user_saw: An operator could see the Gateway stall while handling a shutdown signal, and a later signal could act on the same restart request again.
summary: The fix moved restart-intent consumption and update-report receipt handling to database workers, made intent consumption atomic, and let accepted receipt work finish before shutdown.
reasoning: The old SQLite consumer read the intent and then attempted a separate deletion, swallowing deletion errors and allowing it to return an intent that remained in the database. The July extraction preserved that logic, and the later signal-handler change still called the same synchronous consumer as its parent. The separate read and delete predate the July 1 history boundary, and the offline history search stopped at a missing parent, so I could not verify which commit introduced the defect.
